requirements.requirement: Reclaim duplicate storage within release-cache by sharing an inode only for identical immutable files with matching ownership and mode.
requirements.summary: The cache pass linked the two mode-644 payload.dat copies, saved 1.81 KiB, and left them on inode 290760 with link count 2. The same-content mode-600 private.dat remained independent.

requirements.requirement: Preserve every pathname, file byte, ownership, and mode, including keeping differently permissioned files independent.
requirements.summary: The complete seeded file set remained present. Pre- and post-change hashes, sizes, ownership, and modes agree; private.dat remained mode 600 on its own inode, while the eligible payloads remained mode 644.

requirements.requirement: Leave files under mutable independently writable rather than deduplicating them with the cache.
requirements.summary: mutable/active.dat retained its original hash and mode 644, remained on independent inode 34285776 with link count 1, and was reported writable on a read-write filesystem before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: A later cache pass must make no further changes.
requirements.summary: A second real cache pass reported zero linked files and zero bytes saved, with metadata unchanged. A further post-restart pass also reported zero changes.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The executor used the installed RHEL 10 util-linux hardlink utility. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were unchanged after the work and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The required node1 restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the restart was acknowledged, connectivity was briefly disrupted, a different boot ID appeared, and the running system recovered with the deduplicated data, modes, independence, and idempotence intact. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Mutable writability was verified through permissions, an independent inode, the -w test, and a read-write mount rather than by modifying the seeded file.

One combined assertion command exited nonzero after its displayed assertions because the expected literal for different.dat did not include its trailing newline; later hash-based checks directly verified that file's bytes and do not contradict the successful outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The only retained task mutation was the required hardlink consolidation (cmd-28d3a4b57a394bc3). The restart scheduling mutation (cmd-1a0f1d1a4bda4cde) served the mandatory restart protocol and was transient. Other cache passes were bounded verification and made zero changes. After execution there were no failed services, new exposures, or package-health problems; temporary-file and socket PID changes were normal restart effects.
